Supports junior golf camps and clinics, adult programs, beginner programs, and other player-development initiatives. Prepares instructional areas, equipment, training aids, range balls, and other materials prior to programs and lessons. Assists with participant check-in, group organization, instructional stations, and program transitions. Provides basic instructional feedback to participants under the direction of professional golf staff. Assists with on-course instruction on the Par-3 and regulation golf courses. Helps create a positive, encouraging, safe, and welcoming learning environment for golfers of different ages, abilities, skill levels, and backgrounds. Assists with adaptive golf and other programs designed to make golf accessible to a broad range of participants. Assists staff in developing golf clinics, camps, leagues, lesson plans, instructional activities, and other player-development opportunities. Helps evaluate existing programs and identifies opportunities to improve the participant experience. Supports player-development efforts for juniors, beginners, women, seniors, and other developing golfers. Assists with utilizing the driving range, practice facilities, and Par-3 course as player-development resources. Assists with program registration, participation tracking, attendance, participant feedback, and program evaluation. Supports marketing and communication efforts related to golf programs and instructional opportunities. Maintains clean, organized, safe, and professional instructional and practice areas. Consistently represents the Indian Tree Way – Intentional Hospitality, Operational Excellence, and Making It Work when interacting with participants, guests, and coworkers. OTHER DUTIES/RESPONSIBILITIES:Gains exposure to golf shop operations, outside operations, tee-sheet management, pace of play, tournament operations, customer service, and daily golf course operations. Learns policies and procedures related to golf instruction, course access, range operations, safety, and guest service. Gains an understanding of golf program pricing, budgeting, revenue generation, expense management, and other business aspects of operating a public golf facility. Assists with golf shop and outside operations as assigned to gain a broader understanding of golf facility operations. Works with professional golf staff to establish internship learning goals and participates in ongoing coaching and feedback. May be given increasing responsibility for planning and delivering portions of clinics or instructional programs under the supervision of professional golf staff. Develops practical experience in golf instruction and coaching techniques, junior and adult programming, player development, customer service and hospitality, program management and evaluation, and public-sector golf operations. Performs other duties as assigned. SUPERVISORY DUTIES: This position does not have direct supervisory responsibilities. May assist with organizing and directing participants during camps, clinics, lessons, and other instructional activities under the supervision of professional golf staff. JOB QUALIFICATIONS -KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES:Working knowledge of golf fundamentals, rules, etiquette, and pace of play. Interest in golf instruction, player development, golf operations, and the golf industry. Ability to effectively communicate with children, adults, guests, and coworkers. Strong customer service and interpersonal skills. Ability to create a positive and welcoming experience for program participants. Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a team. Ability to follow direction and work within the scope of assigned responsibilities and training. Ability and willingness to learn, accept coaching and feedback, and demonstrate initiative.Ability to maintain a professional appearance and demeanor. Ability to prioritize participant, guest, and employee safety. Ability to organize equipment and instructional materials and assist with multiple activities and participant groups. Ability to work a flexible schedule that may include mornings, evenings, weekends, and holidays. Ability to consistently demonstrate the principles of the Indian Tree Way – Intentional Hospitality, Operational Excellence, and Making It Work. EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE: Interest in golf instruction, PGA Golf Management, recreation, sports management, education, coaching, or a related field. Working knowledge of golf fundamentals, rules, and etiquette. Experience or demonstrated ability working effectively with children and adults. CPR/AED/First Aid certification or ability to obtain certification as required.Preferred Qualifications: Currently enrolled in or recently graduated from a PGA Golf Management, recreation, sports management, education, kinesiology, business, or related program. Previous experience working at a golf course, driving range, golf camp, recreation program, or instructional setting. Previous experience working with children or youth programs. Interest in pursuing PGA membership or a career in golf instruction, player development, or golf operations.WORK ENVIRONMENT: Work is performed in both indoor and outdoor environments at Indian Tree Golf Club, including the golf shop, driving range, practice facilities, Par-3 course, and regulation golf courses. Work may be performed in varying weather and environmental conditions. The position requires regular interaction with children, adults, program participants, guests, and other employees in an active public recreation environment.PHYSICAL ACTIVITIES: Position requires the ability to stand and walk for extended periods, including walking on uneven outdoor terrain and golf course surfaces. Requires frequent bending, reaching, and movement associated with demonstrating golf skills, setting up instructional areas, and assisting with programs. Must be able to handle, move, and set up golf equipment, training aids, range balls, and other instructional materials and equipment. TRAVEL: Limited travel may be required for meetings, training, programs, or other District-related activities. NOTE: This job description is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, or qualifications associated with the job. May perform other duties as assigned.

jobs.title: Summer 2027 Social Media Internship at Huntington Bank
jobs.description: Employer: Huntington Bank Expires: 10/31/2026 Summary: Huntington’s internship programs provide emerging talent with meaningful, hands‑on experience aligned to their area of study. Over the course of the interns’ time at Huntington, they gain exposure to key business functions across all segments of the organization. An intern’s experience should be focused on professional growth, skill development, and practical application of academic learning. Interns participate in a structured series of development opportunities, including interactions with senior leadership and career pathing insights. The experience also includes immersion in Huntington’s award‑winning culture through community involvement and team‑based activities. Internships at Huntington are designed to help students build a strong foundation for future career success while contributing to meaningful business initiatives. Internship Opportunities at Huntington: Huntington offers internship opportunities for students who are currently enrolled in an academic program and seeking practical, hands‑on experience in their field of study. Internships take place during a defined period of time and are available across all business segments. Rising juniors (Winter 2028 or Spring 2029 grads) may participate in Huntington's Foundations Program, an 8-week, regionally focused experience where students partner directly with a manager and team, contribute to meaningful projects, build professional skills, and explore career opportunities across Huntington and the financial services industry. All interns participate in a variety of developmental and professional activities designed to support learning and exposure to the organization. Depending on your school year, program components may include: Experience in day‑to‑day responsibilities related to their assigned team Exposure to broader business functions A structured schedule of professional development sessions Opportunities to engage with members of the Executive Leadership Team Discussions with senior leaders regarding career paths and Huntington’s business areas A team project focused on applying Huntington’s innovation framework to a business‑relevant problem Participation in volunteer activities and internal events aligned with Huntington’s culture Social Media Internship Overview Huntington Bank is seeking creative, curious and collaborative college students to join our Social Media Internship Program.Eligibility note: This internship is open to rising college juniors enrolled during Summer 2027 at one of the Huntington partner schools for this program: University of Michigan, University of Minnesota, West Virginia University, University of Texas, The Ohio State University, University of Mississippi, University of Alabama or Mississippi State University.This internship offers hands-on experience across the full social media content lifecycle within a highly regulated industry. Interns will join Huntington’s editorial content team and work alongside social media, brand, creative, video and production partners to learn how content moves from initial concept through creation, approval, publication and performance evaluation.Each intern will come from one of Huntington’s partner universities and bring their campus perspective into the program. Working remotely from their home communities, with hybrid in-office participation for Columbus-based interns, interns will contribute ideas, insights and content recommendations that help Huntington connect with customers, communities and university audiences across our footprint. As part of the experience, each intern will develop localized content guidance that reflects their campus, student audience and community context. Duties & Responsibilities: Collaborate with fellow interns and mentors to develop social media concepts grounded in audience needs, business goals, cultural moments and emerging platform opportunities.Participate in brainstorming, creative reviews and content planning discussions by presenting concepts, explaining recommendations and contributing constructive feedback.Work with the editorial content team member who creates and delivers Huntington’s advice and guidance newsletter to identify relevant articles and incorporate them into social plans in ways that are useful, timely and audience-aware.Create, edit, optimize and adapt content for a variety of social platforms and formats, including original photo or video content when opportunities arise and repurposed brand, event or partnership assets.Develop a localized social content toolkit, guide or plan for their Huntington partner university, helping the team understand campus culture, student needs, relevant moments and content opportunities, then present their recommendations to the brand team and other relevant Huntington stakeholders at the end of the internship.Support content planning, workflow management, project execution and performance analysis to help improve future social media content. What You'll LearnContent Strategy, Concept Development & Audience Insight: Learn how leading brands identify audience needs, generate ideas and build content strategies that support business objectives, audience engagement, relevant cultural moments and localized opportunities for Huntington partner universities.Content Creation, Storytelling & Editorial-to-Social Integration: Develop skills in social-first storytelling, content production, copywriting, editing, platform adaptation and content optimization, including how advice and guidance articles can be adapted into useful, timely social plans.Creative Pitching, Collaboration & Feedback: Gain experience presenting ideas, explaining creative rationale, communicating recommendations to peers and stakeholders, and refining work through constructive feedback and collaboration.Project Management: Understand how projects move from concept to completion through planning, timelines, approvals and stakeholder coordination.Brand Standards, Compliance & Reputational Risk: Experience how content is created and reviewed within a regulated financial services environment while balancing strong creative ideas with brand standards, business objectives, risk management and reputational considerations.Measurement & Assessment: Learn how social media content is evaluated and how performance insights are used to improve future content strategies. Required SkillsStrong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present ideas clearly.Enthusiasm for social media and a thoughtful understanding of its value, influence, challenges and responsibility as a public-facing communication channel.Creativity, curiosity and willingness to contribute new ideas.Strong organizational skills, attention to detail and ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.Comfort working independently in a remote environment and collaborating effectively with others.Openness to giving, receiving and incorporating constructive feedback. Preferred SkillsExperience creating content for personal, academic, volunteer, student organization, freelance or professional channels, including social media posts, video, photography, graphics, copywriting or other digital storytelling formats.Comfort using creative tools such as CapCut, Canva, Adobe Creative Suite, Final Cut Pro, in-app editing tools within social platforms or similar platforms to edit, design or adapt content.Interest in how social platforms work, including audience engagement, trends, platform best practices and the role social media can play in building connection, trust and action.Experience contributing to group projects, events, campaigns or creative initiatives, including presenting ideas, collaborating with peers and working toward a shared goal. QualificationsRising college junior enrolled during Summer 2027 at one of the Huntington partner schools for this program: University of Michigan, University of Minnesota, West Virginia University, University of Texas, The Ohio State University, University of Mississippi, University of Alabama or Mississippi State University.Pursuing a degree in Marketing, Communications, Journalism, Media, Advertising, Public Relations, Film, Digital Media or a related field. Application ProcessCandidates selected to advance in the interview process will be asked to complete a brief creative exercise demonstrating their understanding of social media audiences, content strategy and storytelling.

jobs.description: Employer: The Autoimmune Fund Expires: 10/31/2026 Graphic Design Intern: The Autoimmune Decade LaunchPart-time, [10 to 15] hrs/week · [Los Angeles area preferred, remote considered] · $20+/hour, depending on experience · Now through January 2027About usThe Autoimmune Fund is a venture fund dedicated exclusively to autoimmune and immune-mediated disease. Our annual report, The Autoimmune Decade, publishes in December 2026 and launches during JPM Healthcare Week in January 2027. We need a designer to make people notice it.What you’ll makeLaunch campaign. A LinkedIn-first social series: teasers, finding cards, carousels, and event graphics for JPM week.Fund infographics. Turn our findings into visuals people share, not charts for slides.Science visuals. Clear, accurate, original images that explain immunology to investors and patients.How you’ll workThe founder sets the story for each piece. You find the idea and design it. Our creative director reviews and finishes it. You work inside a brand system, and every number comes from our verified research.You haveA portfolio that shows original ideas, not just clean execution. Campaign, editorial, illustration, or motion work all count.Fluency in Figma and/or Adobe IllustratorThe ability to take feedback and revise fastPlus: a biology, health, or science background, or experience in medical or scientific illustrationHow to applySend your portfolio, resume, and response to the prompt below to bonnie@autoimmune.fund with the subject line “Design Intern: [Your Name].” Applications without the prompt will not be reviewed.The Prompt The Autoimmune Decade puts a price on autoimmune disease. It launches in January 2027. Most people scroll past the word “autoimmune.” Your job is to make them stop.1. Find the idea.Sketch three different campaign directions for the launch. Rough is fine: a line, a visual, a thumbnail each. Pick one and tell us in three sentences why it wins.2. Make the hero post.Using your chosen direction, design one finished LinkedIn post (1080 x 1350) built around one of these two facts:From 2014 to 2025, of $40.0 billion in venture capital invested in autoimmune and immune-mediated disease, 94% went to drug therapeutics. Everything else (diagnosis, prediction, devices, care) shared 6%.Women with lupus wait about twice as long as men to be diagnosed: a median of 29.6 months, compared with 14.1 months.3. Explain the science your way.In autoimmune disease, the immune system mistakes the body’s own tissue for a threat. Invent a visual metaphor for that. Show two or three rough options, then finish the one you’d carry forward. In two sentences, tell us where your metaphor breaks down. Every metaphor does somewhere; we want to know you can see it.RulesOriginal work only. No AI-generated imagery, no stock or downloaded icons.Start from our palette: dark green #213E3B, teal #42AA8B, light teal #97D5C2, off-white #F8F8F8. Push it if your idea needs it, and tell us why.Bold idea, disciplined execution. US spelling, no em dashes.Send everything as one PDF. We care more about your thinking than your polish, so include your sketches.

jobs.description: Employer: Playbook Sports Expires: 11/03/2026 About PlaybookPlaybook is the all-in-one, AI-powered operating system for sports and recreation. Camps, clubs, leagues, schools and facilities run their entire business on us: registration, scheduling, payments, marketing, memberships, fundraising and the website that ties it all together.Youth and amateur sports is a massive, passionate market still running on spreadsheets, paper waivers and five disconnected tools. We replace that patchwork with one platform built for how sports orgs actually work, then layer AI on top so a two-person front office can operate like a team of twenty.What makes Playbook different:AI built in, not bolted on. PlayBot, our in-product AI assistant, answers questions and gets admins to the right workflow fast. Our AI-powered email marketing lets orgs send up to 10,000 emails a month free with personalized, automated campaigns.Ready for the agent era. Playbook runs a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server alongside our open REST API, so an org's data is available to AI agents. Very few sports platforms offer this.Grow, not just manage. Smart registration, SEO tools, website builder, marketing automation and Playbook Raise for fundraising help orgs fill programs and grow revenue, not just track it.Run the whole facility. Drag-and-drop bookable calendar, bulk session creation, layered locations, rentals, memberships, passes, payment plans and low-cost ACH.Mobile-first community. The Playbook Connect app keeps parents, players, coaches and staff in sync on iOS and Android.Proof it works. A 15-year NBA veteran used Playbook to grow a single basketball court into a thriving five-court complex, all on one platform. We're rated 4.6/5 on G2.Big-league energy. We host VIP suite events at pro venues for the sports leaders in our markets. Growth here means you'll help pack those suites.Sources: callplaybook.com, Playbook partner profile, AI tools page, G2Why "Founder in Training"This is not a coffee-run internship. You'll sit next to the founders, see the real numbers, and own experiments end to end: idea, build, launch, measure, kill or scale.We call it Founder in Training because the job is to think like an owner. You'll learn how a fast-growing SaaS company finds, wins and keeps customers, and you'll ship things that move the pipeline every single week. If you've ever wanted to start something, this is the closest thing to doing it with a safety net, a playbook (literally) and a team cheering you on.Perform through May and you step into a full-time growth role with a bigger scope, a bigger budget and a seat at the table.What You'll DoEverything you touch ladders up to one goal: more qualified demos and more momentum in our target segments (camps, clubs, leagues, schools and facilities).Content strategyBuild and run a content engine across LinkedIn, short-form video, email and blog that makes sports operators stop scrolling.Turn customer wins, product launches and AI features into stories, case studies and SEO pages that rank and convert.Use AI tools to produce faster and test more angles than a traditional team ever could.Paid adsLaunch, manage and optimize campaigns on Meta, Google and LinkedIn aimed at specific segments and markets.Own the testing loop: creative, audiences, offers, landing pages. Track cost per demo, not just clicks.Build retargeting that brings warm prospects back to book.Conferences and eventsHelp plan and promote our presence at industry conferences, trade shows and our VIP suite events at pro venues.Build pre-event outreach, booth offers and post-event follow-up sequences that turn handshakes into demos.Website and landing page optimizationRun A/B tests on headlines, offers, forms and CTAs to lift conversion on callplaybook.com and campaign pages.Spin up fast, segment-specific landing pages for each campaign, market and vertical.Dig into analytics and session data to find where visitors drop and fix it.Outbound offersDesign irresistible offers (free tools, audits, ROI breakdowns, event invites) that give our sales team a reason to reach out.Build and test outbound sequences with the AE team, and track reply and booking rates by segment.Product-led growthFind ways for the product to sell itself: free tools, freemium hooks, in-app referral loops and self-serve trials.Partner with product and engineering to ship growth experiments, then measure activation and conversion.Leverage tools like our free scheduler and AI email marketing as top-of-funnel magnets.What Success Looks LikeFirst 30 days: You know our segments, product and buyer cold. You've audited our funnel, set up demo tracking by channel, and shipped your first landing page test and content series.By 60 days: You're running paid campaigns with clear cost-per-demo numbers, an outbound offer in market with the AE team, and a weekly growth report the founders actually look forward to.By 90 days: At least one channel or experiment is measurably adding demos every week, and you own a repeatable playbook for it.By May: You've built a growth engine with your fingerprints all over it, shipped a product-led growth initiative, and earned the full-time role.Who You AreYou're scrappy, curious and allergic to "that's how we've always done it." You'd rather run ten small experiments than write one long plan.Must-havesHustle and ownership. You finish what you start and don't wait to be told.Comfort with numbers. You can build a simple funnel, read a dashboard and say what's working.Strong writing. You can make a youth sports director and a facility owner both feel understood.An AI-native mindset. You already use AI tools to research, write, design and build faster.Currently a student, recent grad or early-career builder available through May.Nice-to-havesExperience with Meta, Google or LinkedIn Ads, HubSpot, or landing page tools like Webflow or Unbounce.Video editing or design skills (Canva, CapCut, Figma).A sports background: former athlete, coach, ref, league volunteer or rec-league legend.Something you've started: a side hustle, a club, a newsletter, an online store, anything.What You GetA real path to full time. Crush it through May and the full-time growth role is yours.Founder-level access. Direct mentorship from the people building the company, plus a front-row seat to strategy, sales and product.Real budget, real stakes. You'll spend real ad dollars and own real numbers, not hypothetical ones.Big-league experiences. Help run and attend our VIP suite events at pro sports venues.A portfolio that stands out. Every campaign, page and experiment you ship is yours to show.Impact you can feel. The orgs we serve put kids on fields, courts and ice every day. Helping them grow matters.Compensation, location and hours: [to be added].How to ApplySkip the generic cover letter. Send your resume plus a short note (or a 60-second video) answering one question: If you had $1,000 and 30 days to book more demos for Playbook, what would you do?Bonus points for showing us something you've built, grown or launchedSend email to: james@callplaybook.com

jobs.title: Design Team Intern at The Pennsylvania Horticultural Society
jobs.description: Employer: The Pennsylvania Horticultural Society Expires: 11/04/2026 The Pennsylvania Horticultural Society seeks a Design Team Intern to help bring the 2027 PHS Philadelphia Flower Show to life. This is an exciting, hands-on opportunity to gain professional development and valuable experience in design and event production—with a front-row seat to how one of the country's largest and most celebrated events comes together. Working alongside industry professionals, the intern will assist the Design Team in planning and executing the Flower Show, with a real hand in translating design documentation into on-site reality. It's a role for someone who's equal parts design-minded and logistically sharp, and who likes seeing an idea become something real.The successful candidate manages graphic production and on-site logistical support in a busy special events environment, and can anticipate project needs, prioritize, and meet deadlines with little supervision. They should have a love for design and hands-on problem-solving, be a strong communicator, and be willing to work occasional evenings and weekends during peak Show periods. ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONSReporting to the Director of Planning & Design of the Flower Show, the Design Team Intern will help translate the team’s design drawings into a fully realized physical show, supporting the planning and design process from documentation through on-site execution, including:Graphic & print production: Prepare design files for print, coordinate with print shops, and manage the printing of drawing sets, signage, plant labels, and other graphic materials.Measurement & layout: Take accurate field measurements against construction drawings and help lay out elements throughout the show floor.On-site coordination: Coordinate with labor crews or other teams to assist with accurate organization and placement of elements on site based on planning documents. This may include bulk materials, furniture, signage, and fixturing.Errands & logistics: Run supply and print errands (print shops, hardware stores) using a shared team vehicle.Cross-team support: Jump in with the design, production and site-operations teams on documentation, materials organization, event support, and day-of tasks as they come up.Data > Design: Process and interpret data in Excel and translate spreadsheet information into design outputs (such as diagrams or detail drawings). EDUCATION, EXPERIENCE AND SKILLS REQUIRED:Proficiency in Adobe Creative Cloud programs (InDesign, Photoshop, Illustrator).Proficiency in Microsoft ExcelAbility to create graphic decks in Google Slides.Comfort preparing print and graphic documents.Comfortable using measuring tools (e.g., tape measure) to take accurate measurements.A valid driver’s license and willingness to drive a shared vehicle (minivan).Strong, proactive communicator who is comfortable coordinating with a wide range of people.Possess strong organizational skills and attention to detail.A willingness to iterate and jump in to help the team wherever needed.Bonus: Proficiency in a 3D modeling program—SketchUp and Layout (Trimble) preferred; CAD, Rhino, or similar also welcome. PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS/WORKING CONDITIONS/STIPENDJanuary 11, 2027 – April 23, 2027. Full time at 40 hours/week preferred. Increased hours during the build of the Flower Show as well as during actual show days of the Flower Show.Must be fully available for all hours of the Flower Show period, from set-up to tear-down:Open to Public: 3/12/2027 – 3/21/2027Tear-Down: 3/21/2027 – 3/24/2027Occasional workdays with long hours.Occasional evenings and weekends.Must be able to endure extended periods of walking and/or standing.Must be able to lift 20lbs.Provided a stipend of $3,000 for the duration of their internship.To learn more about us, visit www.phsonline.org or www.theflowershow.comPlease no telephone or walk-in inquiries. EOE. Only those chosen for an interview will be contacted. EEO NOTICE: At PHS, we value a diverse, inclusive workforce and we provide equal employment opportunity for all applicants and employees. All qualified applicants for employment will be considered without regard to an individual’s race, color, sex, gender identity, gender expression, religion, age, national origin or ancestry, citizenship, physical or mental disability, medical condition, family care status, marital status, domestic partner status, sexual orientation, genetic information, military or veteran status, or any other basis protected by federal, state or local laws.

Operating as a creative agency, a strategic consultancy, a sourcing business, and a technology provider, we engage with over 110 million customers every single day for our clients, including McDonald’s, T-Mobile, O2, Starbucks, and adidas. Authenticity and diversity are critical elements of our business. They can only be realized when we create access and equity for all. We know our success is derived from our people, and, as such, we continuously evolve our people practices ensuring personal and professional enrichment, while fostering a work environment that is fun, collaborative, and diverse in thought. tms is seeking an intern to support the Packaging Development team for the term June to December in our headquarters located in downtown Chicago’s West Loop. WHAT YOU WILL BRING TO THE ORGANIZATION Support Packaging Development team members with the following: Developing/testing for new items on our customers’ menusExecuting supplier qualifications for existing packagingDeveloping/testing innovative, compostable packaging alternatives for current packagingExploring cost-savings or operational improvement opportunities through modification of existing packagingExecuting case pack optimization to improve restaurant and/or supplier efficienciesCreate and manage packaging specifications Conduct competitive assessments of food service packaging, assemble reports and present findings to teamSupport consumer Research, focus groups, sensory/kitchen testing set-up, and field testingCoordinate and evaluate 3rdparty lab testing SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE WE WOULD LIKE YOU TO HAVE Successful tms intern candidates meet the following requirements: Pursuing a bachelor’s degree in Packaging Science or relevant fieldCompleted all prerequisite classes to be eligible by start datePrefer a minimum GPA of 3.0Demonstrated time management skills through course work and extracurricular activitiesMS Office proficiency (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Outlook)Excellent written and verbal communicationCollaborative/teamwork oriented EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYERWe are an equal opportunity employer, and we value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, gender, gender expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. jobs.title: Graphic Design Intern at Iowa Natural Heritage Foundation
jobs.description: Employer: Iowa Natural Heritage Foundation Expires: 11/05/2026 Job descriptionAre you a creative individual who enjoys the outdoors and working in a collaborative setting? If so, apply to be part of a small communications team working to help Iowa Natural Heritage Foundation (INHF) protect and restore Iowa’s land, water and wildlife.INHF design interns gain real-world experience designing professional-quality publications, logos and graphics. The design intern works across departments to create print and digital collateral, display and marketing materials, and complete special projects. Design interns gain experience working within an established brand and representing that brand to in-person and digital audiences.Work examplesThe design intern will contribute to INHF’s quarterly magazine, annual calendar, outreach materials, project mailings, event collateral, web and social media graphics among other projects. Depending on skills and interest, other marketing, video and/or photography work may be included.Skills/QualificationsThis position usually goes to graphic design majors, journalism majors specializing in visual design or students with strong design/web experience and coursework. Knowledge of Adobe Creative Suite software is required. Experience with Squarespace, WordPress or other web content building platforms. All programs and equipment (with the exception of a personal computer if working remotely) provided by INHF.We’re looking for students who are:Interested in climate solutions, the outdoors, land protection and/or stewardshipAttentive to detailCreative, with a passion for visual designEnjoy seeking out and learning about new techniques and trendsFlexible, organized and capable of working on multiple projects with varying deadlinesComfortable collaborating with a teamThis internship is open to undergraduate students who live in or are attending a college, university or technical program in Iowa. AvailabilityTiming for this internship can be flexible with school schedules. Preference will be given to applicants who can start in January of 2027, working between 10-15 hours/week, and continuing through the summer. In the summer, interns must be available to work 32 hours/week. The internship will end in August. Pay is $15/hr. Most work will be done in the INHF office, but there will be opportunities to work remotely, assist at outreach events and visit project sites in the field. Interns must provide their own transportation to and from work, if needed. INHF encourages interns to take advantage of active and mass transit options while in the Des Moines metro area (DART system, biking and carpooling).Application informationApplication deadline is November 4, 2026. Applications should include:A one-page cover letterResume5-6 samples of your work (published/professional examples are ideal, but classroom work is also accepted). Work samples can be in a PDF or Word document format or through a link(s) (for example, to an online portfolio). One letter of recommendation from a professor or professional in your major/area of interest. The letter may be included in your application or sent separately by the author. Please include reference contact information.

jobs.title: 2027 TFC Summer Internship - Audio Visual Production at The Freeman Company
jobs.description: Employer: The Freeman Company Expires: 11/05/2026 About UsThe Freeman Company is a global leader in events, on a mission to redefine live for a new era. With a data-driven approach and the industry’s largest network of experts, The Freeman Company's insights shape exhibitions, exhibits, and events that drive audiences to action. The integrated full-service solutions leverage a 99-year legacy in event management as well as new technologies to deliver moments that matter.SummaryTFC Summer Internship Experience - May 24th to July 30th Are you a student interested in audio, video, lighting, live production, or event technology and curious about what happens behind the scenes to bring a live event to life? Join Freeman for a 10-week summer internship experience where you'll gain hands-on exposure to the live events industry. You'll contribute to real projects, learn alongside industry professionals, build your network, and participate in professional development throughout the summer. As an intern within Freeman Audio Visual (FAV), you'll work alongside Freeman's production and operations teams to learn how technology, people, and planning come together to deliver live experiences for our customers. Education & ExperienceWhat We're Looking ForWe're looking for students who are excited by technology, enjoy hands-on environments, and want to explore a career in live event production. jobs.title: TV News Internship at KSNW TV
jobs.description: Employer: KSNW TV Expires: 11/05/2026 KSN is looking for an upper-level college student who is ready to jump into the world of TV news. We are looking for someone who has taken journalism classes and has some writing experience. Experience with collegiate TV production is not necessary, but great if you have it! Previous experience with print-based journalism also a plus. Internship will include working with multiple team members to learn many different skills in the newsroom (including shadowing producers, reporters, photographers, editors and other newsroom team members). After an initial training process, internship will have a specific focus of photojournalism (shooting and editing video), multi-media journalism (shooting and editing video, writing stories for broadcast and digital) and/or producing newscasts (editing video, stacking newscasts, writing for broadcast and digital) based on the skills and experience of the individual intern. Some sports coverage is expected for those who shoot and edit video (focusing on high school football). Position is for 2026/27 semesters to be determined, located in Wichita, Kansas, and will remain open until filled. There is no “normal” schedule in a newsroom, so expect to work odd hours, including weekends, early mornings, or evenings. We will coordinate your class schedule with your weekly internship schedule. We have hired some of our previous rock-star interns for full-time work – this is a great way to get your foot in the door!Internship Details :Each internship is for 15-20 hours per week for approximately 15-20 weeks Will be well supervised and participate in a meaningful learning experience Upon completion of the internship, the student will be evaluated by the internship supervisor Requirements & Skills :Must be a college junior/senior with multiple journalism classes completed Expected to work 2-3 shifts per week, hours may vary A collaborative worker with a willingness to learn Previous internship experience a plus, but not required Fluency in English, bilingual Spanish a plus Collegiate experience in news writing is required; can include AP Style writing for college newspaper, script writing for broadcast, or related assignments #LI-OnsiteSCAM ALERT:Please be aware candidates may be at risk of being targeted by scammers seeking personal data or money. Recruiters with Nexstar Media Group and its local stations will only contact you through official job boards, LinkedIn, or email with Nexstar.tv domain or official station email addresses (example:@wreg.com). Be cautious of any outreach claiming to be from Nexstar or its recruiters via any other messaging platforms or personal email addresses. We will not contact you using a @gmail email address. If you are unsure about the authenticity of a job inquiry or offer, email us at corporaterecruiters@nexstar.tv.

jobs.feedName: Mike Curb College of Arts, Media, & Communication
jobs.title: Social Media Content Intern at The Spellbound Group
jobs.description: Employer: The Spellbound Group Expires: 11/05/2026 The Spellbound Group is a social media and marketing agency working with artists, legacy estates, and lifestyle brands. We run day-to-day social, write copy, build campaigns, and report on what's working for clients across music and beyond. Our roster spans contemporary artists and some of the most storied catalogs in music, including Janis Joplin Juan Gabriel, The Doors, Henry Mancini, and John Lee Hooker, plus our parent company's affiliated brands like Trixie Mattel, Hilary Duff, Huddy, Katya, Masego, Nickelback, Zedd, Luke Hemmings, Megadeth, and more. That means one week you might be cutting a tour recap and the next you're finding a fresh way to introduce a classic album to a new generation. ** Must be in Philadelphia. This position is 95% remote, but our office is in Philadelphia, and we may need you to come into the office once or twice in a while to film content or attend a meeting. We're hiring a paid Social Media Content Intern with strong video editing skills and a knack for creative planning. You'll work closely with our creative team to turn raw footage, archival assets, and campaign ideas into short-form content that performs. This is a hands-on role. Your edits will go live on real client channels, and your ideas will shape what we post. What you'll do • Edit short-form video for Instagram Reels, TikTok, YouTube Shorts, and Facebook, including captions, text overlays, music sync, and platform-specific cutdowns • Turn live footage, interviews, behind-the-scenes clips, and archival material into polished, on-brand posts • Help plan monthly content calendars and pitch creative concepts for campaigns, releases, anniversaries, and tours • Adapt one piece of content into multiple formats and aspect ratios • Keep an eye on trends, sounds, and formats and suggest ways our clients can use them authentically • Organize and tag footage and assets so the team can find what they need fast • Support photo selection, simple graphics, and light copywriting as needed • Help pull performance insights for monthly reports and learn what makes content work What we're looking for • Strong video editing skills in Premiere Pro, Final Cut, DaVinci Resolve, CapCut, or similar • A portfolio or reel showing short-form social content you've edited • A good sense of pacing, music, and storytelling in under 60 seconds • Creative planning instincts and the ability to pitch ideas clearly • Solid organization and the ability to hit deadlines while working remotely • Comfort taking feedback and turning revisions around quickly Nice to have • Experience with Canva, Photoshop, or After Effects • Familiarity with scheduling tools and platform analytics • A love of music, from current artists to classic catalogs • Currently studying or recently graduated in film, media, communications, marketing, or a related field

jobs.feedName: Mike Curb College of Arts, Media, & Communication
jobs.title: Design & Production Intern at Cellsense
jobs.description: Employer: Cellsense Expires: 11/06/2026 Design & Production Intern Brooklyn, NY | On-site DescriptionCellsense transforms algae and cellulose into sustainable beads and beaded fabrics for the fashion, jewelry, and beauty industries. Cellsense’s proprietary material replaces sources of microplastics and heavy-metal pollution while offering designers a wide range of brilliant colors, clarity, and properties such as fluorescence. Our innovative manufacturing system cuts lead time of customized beaded products from weeks to days by eliminating expensive tooling and tedious manual labor from conventional processes. Currently, we are focused on scaling up our process while engaging in paid pilots with industry partners. We recently closed our pre-seed round and have received inbound interest from 55+ companies. You would be joining at a particularly exciting stage of growth. OpportunityAs a Design and Production Intern at Cellsense, you will immerse yourself in hands-on development and production of our bio-based embellishments and beaded fabric. This position offers a unique opportunity to collaborate closely with designers, engineers, fashion, jewelry, and cosmetic brands, contributing to innovative projects aimed at advancing sustainable materials.We are looking for a hands-on creative who loves making things. You will be at the center of how our bio-embellishments and beaded fabrics come to life. This role involves design, trend forecasting, and physical making. You’ll turn research trends, conceptualize designs, and then physically create the high-quality prototypes that we present to the world’s most recognized fashion and beauty brands. If you are passionate about shaping the future of sustainable materials and love the tactile process of bringing ideas into the physical world, this role is for you.Key ResponsibilitiesAssist in the assembly and production of finished pieces, tracking progress and ensuring consistent qualityExperiment with design ideas, color palettes, and fabrication methods, translating these explorations into tangible product improvementsPhotograph progress and completed samples, keeping organized records and contributing to our visual narrative on digital platformsCollaborate on social media and website content to share our production milestones and material innovationsBrainstorm process improvements that enhance efficiency and throughputWork closely with cross-functional teams, ensuring our materials meet both aesthetic and market needsQualificationsCurrently pursuing a degree in industrial design, product design, textiles, fashion, jewelry, or a related field.Familiarity with Adobe Creative Cloud and other design tools.An eye for aesthetics and a keen interest in emerging fashion and material trends.Comfortable juggling multiple projects, with strong attention to detail and craftsmanship.Enthusiastic about sustainable materials and eager to help shape a more responsible design ecosystem.Benefits$18/hrAccess to a fully equipped office and manufacturing spaceThe chance to join a collaborative team pushing the boundaries of sustainable materials, directly impacting both the environment and emerging markets.

jobs.description: Employer: BodyStories: Teresa Fellion Dance Expires: 11/07/2026 WHO ARE WE?BodyStories: Teresa Fellion Dance is an NYC-based non-profit contemporary dance company of womxn and non-binary individuals, officially formed in 2011, and active with individual projects since 2004. We create original dance works in collaboration with composers and artists of all disciplines, and have performed across the continental United States, Cameroon, Dubai, and in Europe at venues such as Jazz at Lincoln Center, Bryant Park Fallstage, Baryshnikov Arts Center, ICA Boston, Gibney Dance Center, ENTPE Lyon, France, with the rock band Phish, and others. We work very closely with our Musical Director, John Yannelli, to make each BodyStories performance a unique sensory experience, upholding our mission to create profound emotional responses for our audiences. In addition to creating and performing innovative works, our company is committed to connecting with diverse populations through our extensive dance education programs and community engagement workshops, as well as maintaining a stable business model to sustain our work. We collectively speak nine languages and research, perform, and collaborate with artists from five continents. In addition to our in-person education and performance programming, we have launched a virtual dance education program and several online performance programs, and are continuing to develop offerings. Previous arts administration experience preferred. In addition to the following areas of focus, interns will perform general operational tasks and take on other exciting projects involved in several aspects of our BodyStories Spring 2027 programming. MARKETING & MEDIA INTERNManage company social media accounts (Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok)Photo/video editingWork with Artistic Director to develop and execute marketing campaigns in relation to company events and projectsWork with Company Manager and development team to design and implement fundraising campaignsNewsletter and correspondence designDesign of print and online marketing materials(Experience with Photoshop and Illustrator is preferred) SPECIAL EVENTS & DEVELOPMENT INTERNMonthly newsletter and communicationsContent developmentWork with Company Manager to plan and coordinate donor cultivation eventsResearch and apply for residencies and performance opportunitiesResearch touring locations and venuesTouring correspondence assistanceGrant application assistanceCorporate sponsorship assistanceARTS MANAGEMENT INTERNResearch rental space availabilities and book rehearsalsMonthly newsletter and communicationsAssist with scheduling for special eventsAssist with scheduling for company events and rehearsalsWork with Company Manager and Artistic Director Assist with recruiting and scheduling for dance education programAssist with correspondence with dance students, arts organizations, and artistsGeneral administrative assignmentsContent developmentIn-person, Remote, Hybrid OptionsOur internships have traditionally involved a combination of remote and in-person work. Because of the COVID-19 crisis, we shifted to an entirely remote work environment. As the COVID-19 situation evolves, we currently have remote, hybrid, and in-person options. A fully remote internship is completely possible, and remote and in-person candidates are equally encouraged to apply. jobs.title: Change Academy Internship at Marketing for Change
jobs.description: Employer: Marketing for Change Expires: 11/07/2026 Spring 2027: Change Academy Internship & Fellowship (Orlando, FL & Alexandria, VA + Denver, CO is design only) DescriptionThe Change Academy at Marketing for Change offers graduate students, college seniors and others a paid semester-long experience working and learning at one of the nation’s leading behavior-change marketing agencies. In behavior-change marketing, the objective is not sales or profits; it’s influencing behaviors in a way that leads to a healthier, safer, more sustainable world. Each semester, the Change Academy accepts three to five interns with demonstrated skills or education in marketing, advertising, writing, research, and graphic design. Interns work together with experts in their field on real-life projects and also receive both skill-specific and broader training in behavioral science. Interns participate in agency events, client meetings and (if you want) off-the clock social gatherings. Interns earn $18.40 an hour or minimum wage (whichever is higher) and work 20 hours a week, with at least one day a week in our offices. The in-office experience is critical to help interns improve their skills, work with mentors and share a group experience with other interns in their cohort. Please confirm you can participate in person at your selected location. LocationOur offices are located in Orlando and just outside Washington, DC, and we very much prefer to hire people willing to locate in those areas. Additionally, we have a design hub in the Denver area. We are mostly a hybrid workforce with staff working together in-person at least one day a week because we value the fun and collaboration that allows. The program lasts between 12 and 16 weeks depending on the semester. Instruction takes place during the first 6 to 8 weeks of the internship, mixed with group projects and real work experience. The final weeks focus on work experience and give applicants an opportunity to build an impressive portfolio. Select interns may also be asked to apply as fellows, who can work up to 40 hours a week, or to join the Marketing for Change team permanently as employees. The Change Academy is the main path to entry-level employment at Marketing for Change. Several former M4C interns are now in leadership roles at M4C, including an art director, creative director, senior media planner, and strategist.Requirements Relevant experience or college classes in a related field. Preference is given to graduate students, recent graduates or college seniors with at least one prior internship in a relevant field. Other adults with the right skills but no degree may also apply. (Several have been successful in the past.)Deep curiosity in what makes people tick.An interest in using your powers for good and making the world a better place.Being a nice person. Seriously. We want the kind of person most other people love to work with. A quick note about our hiring processApplying for a job can feel a little like sending your application out into the void and hoping a real person is on the other side. At Marketing for Change, one will be. Real people on our team review every application. We may use technology to make parts of the process easier, but when it comes to getting to know you, considering what you could bring to our team and making hiring decisions, that’s us. We know there’s a real person on the other side of every application, too. Someone who gave us their time, shared a little bit of their story and decided we might be worth exploring. We don’t take that lightly. And if you’re considering us, we’re genuinely glad you’re here. Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States. Employment is contingent upon the successful completion of a background check and Form I-9 Employment Eligibility Verification. Please submit your application by November 1, 2026, to be considered for this opportunity. We look forward to learning more about you! Location & TimingJanuary 2027 - May 2027 | Orlando, FL & Alexandria, VA + Denver, CO (design only)

jobs.description: Employer: STORExpress Expires: 11/08/2026 Historical Timeline Exhibit Designer / Graphic DesignerProject: Design of a Professional Historical Timeline Display Location: Pittsburgh, PA / Remote Project Type: FreelanceAbout the ProjectSTORExpress is developing a series of professional historical displays for several of its storage facilities throughout the Pittsburgh region. Each display will tell the story of the building and surrounding property, from its earliest history through its industrial use and eventual redevelopment by STORExpress.We are looking for a graphic designer, exhibit designer, museum designer, or similar creative professional who can transform our completed historical research, photographs, maps, documents, and written captions into a polished, visually engaging physical exhibit.This is not simply a digital timeline or infographic. The finished product should look and feel like a small, professional museum or historical exhibit.What We NeedThe designer will help develop the visual design and layout for a large-format historical timeline display. The display may include:A chronological timeline of the property’s historyHistorical photographs and documentsMaps and architectural/property imagesHistorical newspaper clippings and advertisementsShort historical narratives and captionsImportant dates and eventsArtifacts and artifact display areasSTORExpress redevelopment historyVisual connections between different periods of the property's historySupporting graphics, decorative elements, and typographyThe final display will be printed on physical panels and installed inside a STORExpress facility. One of our current displays is approximately 15 feet wide by 7 feet tall, so experience designing for large physical spaces is highly desirable.What We Already HaveWe have already completed much of the historical research. We will provide:Historical information and written contentPhotographsMapsDocuments and archival materialDates and timeline informationHistorical captionsResearch sources/citationsDirection on the historical story we want the display to tellExamples and inspiration for the overall lookYou will not be expected to conduct the historical research from scratch. Your primary responsibility is to turn our existing research and materials into a cohesive, professional exhibit design.The Look We Are Going ForWe want the finished product to feel closer to a museum exhibit or historical center than a corporate infographic.We are looking for a design that is:ProfessionalClean and sophisticatedHistorically appropriateVisually interestingEasy to read from a distanceEngaging for visitors of different agesCapable of incorporating a large amount of historical information without feeling clutteredDesigned specifically for a physical wall/display rather than simply a screenWe particularly like displays that use a strong visual timeline, large historical photographs, archival materials, maps, layered information, and carefully designed typography.Scope of WorkThe initial project will involve designing one complete prototype display based on our existing research.The selected designer would be expected to:Review our historical research and existing draft.Develop an overall visual concept and layout.Create the timeline structure and hierarchy.Incorporate our photographs, documents, maps, and written content.Design areas for physical artifacts where appropriate.Produce a professional, print-ready design.Make revisions based on our feedback.Provide final files suitable for professional large-format printing.If the initial prototype is successful, there is potential for additional displays for other STORExpress locations. We currently anticipate approximately 16 locations eventually requiring historical displays.Ideal CandidateWe would especially like to hear from people with experience in:Museum exhibit designHistorical exhibit designEnvironmental graphic designLarge-format graphic designExhibition designArchitectural graphicsBrand/environmental designHistorical society or cultural institution projectsInformation designLarge-scale print productionA strong graphic designer without museum experience may also be a good fit if they can demonstrate excellent large-format design and visual storytelling.What to Include in Your ResponsePlease send:A short description of your experienceYour portfolio or examples of relevant workAny examples of museum, historical, exhibition, or large-format projectsYour estimated price for designing one displayYour estimated timelineWhether you can provide print-ready filesAny relevant experience working with large physical installationsPlease do not send only examples of logos, social media graphics, or standard digital marketing materials. We are primarily interested in seeing examples of large-format, exhibit, environmental, editorial, or information-based design.ImportantWe are looking for someone who can take a large amount of historical information and make it visually compelling without losing the story.The goal is for visitors to stop, look at the display, and understand that the building they’re in has a real history.This is a long-term project with the possibility of additional work if the first display is successful.

jobs.description: Employer: MACOM Expires: 11/09/2026 MACOM (NASDAQ: MTSI) is a global leader in the design and manufacture of advanced semiconductor products across a diverse range of end markets, including Data Centers, Telecommunications, Industrial and Aerospace and Defense. We develop innovative, cutting-edge technologies and products across the spectrum of radio frequency (RF), microwave, millimeter wave, photonics and high-speed analog technologies. Our solutions support critical network infrastructure applications like artificial intelligence, high performance computing, satellite communications, radar, unmanned aerial vehicles, medical equipment, test and measurement and advanced wireless networks. MACOM has more than 75 years of expertise in semiconductor process development, wafer fabrication, circuit design, advanced packaging, systems architecture and applications engineering. We are committed to our customers’ success. We partner with customers to help solve their most challenging problems by providing semiconductor solutions that are at the forefront of the highest power, highest frequency and/or highest data rates. Leading technologies, innovative products and driven employees. Come be a part of MACOM and help advance the next generation of connectivity infrastructure! Technical Project Analyst: PMO & Security OperationsThe Team & Your RoleThis role sits at the intersection of project execution and information security operations. You will support MACOM's Information Security team by helping build out a PMO function, covering the dashboards that track security initiatives, the processes that keep projects on schedule, and the standards that scale the program over time. This position is designed to develop well-rounded project management skills, with the expectation that you will grow into independently managing projects as you gain experience. Core Responsibilities• Develop and apply core project management skills including scope definition, scheduling, risk tracking, and stakeholder communication across active security initiatives.• Support project managers in planning and executing projects, with increasing ownership over time as skills and familiarity with the team's portfolio grow.• Build and maintain PMO dashboards and reporting tools in Power BI, Airtable, ServiceNow, or similar platforms to provide real-time visibility into project status, milestones, resource utilization, and risk across the security portfolio.• Support the Information Security team in tracking deliverables, deadlines, dependencies, and action items across concurrent initiatives.• Collect, clean, and synthesize project data from multiple sources to produce accurate and actionable status reports for stakeholders.• Assist in coordinating cross-functional meetings, capturing meeting minutes, and following up on open items to maintain project momentum.• Contribute to the design and documentation of PMO processes, templates, and governance standards that will serve as the foundation of the program.• Identify gaps in current project tracking workflows and recommend tooling or process improvements to increase team efficiency.• Support the evaluation and potential implementation of PPM (Project Portfolio Management) tooling to centralize and scale program visibility across the security organization. Qualifications• Pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Business, Information Systems, Engineering Management, Cybersecurity, or a related field.• Familiarity with project management concepts (e.g., Agile, Waterfall, or hybrid methodologies).• Experience building dashboards or reports using tools such as Power BI, Airtable, Excel, or similar platforms.• Strong organizational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to manage multiple tasks simultaneously.• Nice to Have: Exposure to PPM or work management tools (e.g., ServiceNow, Smartsheet, Jira, Monday.com, MS Project), basic familiarity with information security concepts, and knowledge of data visualization best practices. During the 12 weeks each Intern will:• Be given an individual and well-defined project with set outcome goals• Gain hands on experience• Receive excellent training and ongoing supervision• Be invited to attend an intern webinar series• Attend networking/social events• Attend and present at Poster Session about each Interns project successes and pitfalls• Receive formal, written feedback The Hourly Range for this position is $20 – $47 per hour. MACOM will not discriminate against any worker or job applicant on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, military service, marital status, or any other category protected under applicable law. jobs.description: Employer: Genuine Parts Company Expires: 11/09/2026 Job DescriptionJob Summary Are you ready to spend your summer as a part of something special? Imagine being with a company whose reputation for excellence paves the way for endless success. At Genuine Parts Company (GPC), people build long-lasting, highly satisfying careers and make a real difference in the community. Our 10-week summer internship program will be in person in Atlanta and run from May 24 – July 30, 2027. As an Assortment Planning Intern, you will be developing an Assortment Engine that optimizes SKU productivity across all Napa locations. Our internship program is designed as a cohort experience, bringing interns from across the organization together to learn, grow, and build connections throughout the summer. While gaining hands-on experience within your team, you'll also be part of a community of fellow interns sharing the journey alongside you. As an intern at GPC, you can look forward to: Meaningful Work: Contribute to projects that support key business priorities and showcase your impact through a final presentation to senior leaders. Professional Development: Participate in development experiences designed to build your skills, confidence, and understanding of the workplace. Leadership Exposure: Hear from and connect with leaders across the organization, including senior executives, to learn more about our business, leadership, and career growth. jobs.title: Visuals Systems and AI Design Intern at The Autoimmune Fund
jobs.description: Employer: The Autoimmune Fund Expires: 11/09/2026 About The Autoimmune FundAutoimmune and immune-mediated diseases affect millions of people, most of them women. Yet the money has gone almost entirely one way. Of the $40.0 billion in venture funding that went to the field from 2014 to 2025, 94.4% went to drug therapeutics. Prediction, diagnostics, devices, care access, monitoring and remission maintenance shared the remaining 5.6%. The Autoimmune Fund, a seed and Series A venture fund dedicated exclusively to autoimmune and immune-mediated disease, exists to back the rest.We invest across the whole spectrum of care. We lead investments everywhere except drug therapeutics, where we co-invest. Our thesis follows three scientific revolutions reshaping the field: Immune Precision, Accelerated Aging, and Female Biology.We are a small team that runs on AI. Everything we publish, from The Autoimmune Decade, our annual report launching in January 2027, to our slides, one-pagers and infographics, runs on one visual system. We want that system to be precise enough that an AI can apply it as reliably as a trained designer. What You'll DoYou will own how the fund looks, and teach an AI to hold that standard.First project: align our visual communication system. Audit our palette, typography, icons, chart styles, grids and layout rules across documents and slides. Find where they conflict, propose the rulings, and turn the result into one clear, written source of truth with components ready to use.Second project: train Claude on our design system. Set up our brand inside Claude's design tools (Claude Design) and write the instructions and reusable skills that teach it our rules. Generate slides, one-pagers and infographics, compare them against the standard, find where the AI drifts, and fix the instructions until it stops.Then: extend the system as the fund grows. Carry the system and its AI workflows into new formats, including report exhibits, social posts and web pages, so every piece we publish looks like it came from one hand. You HaveCurrent enrollment in an undergraduate program in design, visual communication, HCI, or a related fieldA portfolio that shows at least one system, such as a brand identity, type system or component library, not only single piecesReal typographic judgment: pairing, hierarchy, grids, and setting numbers so they alignDiscipline with a constrained palette, including contrast and accessibilityAdvanced Figma: components, styles and variables, not just drawingReal, hands-on AI use. You've built prompts, custom instructions, projects or workflows in tools like Claude or ChatGPT, and you can show us oneClear writing. Training an AI is mostly turning taste into precise, testable rulesAvailability to work in person in Los Angeles Nice to HaveCoursework or lab experience in immunology, biology or another life scienceData visualization experienceBasic HTML/CSS or MarkdownInterest in healthcare, biotech or venture capital What You'll GetDirect mentorship. You work side by side with the fund's Managing Partner, a clinician and former Wall Street healthcare equity analyst who covered 500+ companies over 14 years.Work that ships. What you build goes into real investor materials and our annual report, not a drawer.Builder-level AI skills. You will design, test and fix AI systems, not just prompt them.A front-row seat to venture. See how a specialist fund sources companies, weighs science and makes decisions.A portfolio piece few undergrads have. A working design system and the AI that applies it, both built by you. To ApplySend your resume, a portfolio with at least one system project, and a short note (200 words max) describing one design rule you once had to make precise enough for someone else to follow, and what went wrong the first time to bonnie@autoimmune.fund. Work Test (3 to 4 hours, unpaid)We'll send you a packet: an excerpt of our brand rules, three past pieces of ours, and two pages of raw content (Content A and Content B). Send everything back as one PDF plus your instruction file. Unfinished parts are fine if you tell us what you would do next.1. Rule the conflicts. Our rules and our past pieces do not fully agree. List every conflict you find. For each, state the rule you would adopt and why, in one sentence. Flag anything else in the packet you think is wrong.2. Design the standard. Design a one-pager from Content A in Figma or a similar tool, by hand, with no AI-generated imagery. This is the reference the AI must match.3. Teach the AI. Write one set of instructions (a skill, custom instructions or a system prompt) that gets an AI to produce Content B in the same system. The same instructions must work on both pages. No hand edits to the AI output.4. Score it. Write at least ten pass/fail checks for this system. Score your AI output against them. An honest 7 out of 10 beats an inflated 10 out of 10.5. Show the work. Share the full chat log. In 150 words or fewer, tell us where the AI failed and what that taught you about writing instructions.

jobs.description: Employer: Camp Augusta Expires: 11/09/2026 Arts Educator and Camp CounselorLocation: Northern California (onsite housing provided)Position Type: Full-time, seasonal (May 18th-August 14th)Compensation: From $4500 + food, housing, utilities, training, and perks!Love learning new skills, designing magical spaces, and bringing a world of creativity to youth? Interested in developing your art skills and growing into a leadership role with kids and adults in a personal and professionally growth-centered community? We might just have the perfect role for you! Camp Augusta runs over 30 different art activities at our camp, with many that are far and above most camp arts programs. The domain is managed by an Arts Director, who helps to train, manage, budget, and inventory for everything that goes into this domain. The main facilitators of these clinics are counselors, whose role is the bread and butter in bringing the art experience to campers in facilitation and mentorship. Both are directly involved in arts education, and an opportunity for professional development would be the counseling to arts director track. :)Art Educator Positions:The Counselor position offers a summer salary $5000, and includes a significant amount of learning, teaching, practicing, and getting involved in the many wonderful aspects of camp, with opportunities for growth into an Arts Director role in future years. Apply to Camp Augusta, and by the end of August, your resume could read:Intensive Art Facilitator and Camp Counselor - Camp Augusta Summer 2027After 300+ hours of dedicated training, including in intensive arts like blacksmithing, ceramics, glass working, jewelry smithing, and more, I acted as an arts domain leader as well as the primary caretaker for 5 campers with 24-hour responsibilities including behavior management and child development. Skills of practice include facilitation and debriefing, Non-Violent Communication, performance arts, 1st aid / emergency preparedness, and teaching various activity areas.Internships?Yup, we do that. We can co-design your internship based on the skills and development you seek, and the specific requirements of your school!Note: Some educational institutions require prior approval before the start of an internship. It is the responsibility of the student to check with their institution to be sure they meet any requirements before they accept a position.Art Educator Skills and Qualities:Love of Youth – Mentoring kiddos (and staff) in a safe, fun, and directed manner.Organized – Keeping all the arts stocked, organized, systematized, and orderly.Community-Minded – A creator of optimism and energy in the community.Camp-Minded – Excitement to engage with the larger camp community to offer fun, memorable experiences even beyond the realm of the arts program (evening programs, story experiences, Playstations, and more)About Being a Counselor:After the training and preparation, the campers arrive for either 1 or 2-week sessions in our 9-week summer. Discover the wish, wonder, and surprise of living with and supporting five campers in a cabin in the woods, and learn more than you ever thought you could about relating to children in a manner that empowers their growth and independence. In a single day at camp, you'll:Create magical, intentional special wake ups and evening connection-building activities for your cabin on a daily basisFacilitate camper ideas for a daily creative cabin activityTeach four activity blocks per day from the 150 clinics that you chose to learn in trainingRun a unique, themed daily activity that draws upon your personal creativity and skills; “sell” these activities through playful skitsPlay in epic Evening Programs, from full-camp capture the flag to immersive nighttime events. Be a character in our games and bring other-worldly magic to life.Create and offer two gifts from the heart per camper, per session: a special wood cookie honoring and a thoughtful Parent LetterCounselors are the heartbeat of camp. Most counselors spend a session or two outside of the cabin as well, contributing to programming or other areas of interest. See our page on counselor life for more information on the role and how it differs from most other camps. Minimum requirementsMust be at least 19 years of age by June 1st, 2027Must be available during our summer dates: from May 18th to August 14th 2027 (if within a couple days, inquire)AND MUST have one of the following: At least one summer of experience at a summer campOver 100 hours of direct mentorship work with youthA major or background directly related to working with youth, with intention to work with youth in your futurePreferred qualifications:A history of ‘meaningful’ work and a variety of experiences with youthA plethora of interesting hobbies, passions, and life experiences that you’re excited to share with usA GPA of 3.0+ with a true excitement for learning and writing Benefits of working at Camp Augusta: 300+ Hours of Experiential Training: Pre-arrival preparation and 3.5 weeks of on-site training, including:75+ hours of experiential learning in psychology, sociology and education-based philosophies and approaches45+ hours learning activities within our 150+ clinic offerings180+ hours of learning camp by doing camp9 Weeks of Summer Practicing: Being responsible for cabins of 5 campers at a time, and applying all the skills above to camp activities and discussions.A Skilled & Dedicated Scaffolder: With no more than a 1:8 ratio, this person emphasizes your growth and works with you to develop your skills working with kidsPaid & Inclusive: This position offers a summer salary of $5000. Additional opportunities for pre-and post-season work also exist. All work includes freshly-prepared organic food, housing, and many more Perks and Benefits.About Camp Augusta:Camp Augusta is a nonprofit residential summer camp in northern California that offers a truly unique summer camp experience for campers and staff alike. We are focused on counseling skills, creativity, excellent programming, and camper choice - see more about the vision of our camp here.We aim to include and celebrate many facets of human identity – gender identity and expression, sexual orientation, religion, ethnicity, race, age, neurodiversity, disability status, citizenship, and other aspects that make us unique. We are working to craft an inclusive culture founded on ideals of curiosity, honesty, empathy, and acceptance – a place where people are seen and acknowledged for their shared humanity as well as their unique individuality.
